method: We filtered every ENERGY STAR certified residential clothes dryer to those whose certification record flags heat pump technology (hybrid heat pump models excluded), kept the full-size ventless models only (compact dryers are certified on a smaller test load, so their yearly kWh is not comparable), merged identical models sold under several brand names, and ranked on certified Combined Energy Factor (CEF, 95% of the score); the shorter DOE test cycle makes up the other 5%, so dryers with the same CEF are ordered by cycle length. Yearly kWh is ENERGY STAR's own estimate for DOE's 283 test loads; we price it at the EIA U.S. average residential rate and multiply by five. We did not test any dryer. A dryer that dries faster in the DOE test can still take longer in your home: the test uses a fixed load and moisture target. The Midea MLE27N5AWWC certifies a CEF of 10.14 as a standard ventless dryer but its record carries no heat pump flag; we follow the record and leave it out. The LG WashTower stacked dryer is also certified but is left out of the ranking because LG lists it as discontinued. The Beko HPD24414W and the Blomberg DHP24404W3 listed near the top appear to be the same Arcelik machine in an earlier and a later revision (this page's sold-as record lists the later number as also sold as the Beko model); ENERGY STAR certifies them separately and their certified figures differ only in test cycle length, so treat them as one choice. The LG DLHC5502 and DLHC6702 are certified heat pump dryers that are not ranked because we could not confirm their seller page.
name: The most efficient full-size heat pump dryers, ranked by certified CEF with the yearly cost to run
scoring: each value scored against the best on the page (best = 1), times its weight; total out of 100

excluded.filter: no heat pump flag in the certification record
excluded.why: heat pump dryers only: 'ventless' is not the same thing (ventless dryers without a heat pump typically certify far lower, a median CEF of 2.68 against 3.93 for vented dryers), so the heat pump flag in the certification record is the filter, and hybrid heat pump models (a different design, median CEF 4.5) are left out
sold in Canada only: this page prices electricity at the U.S. average rate, so Canada-only listings are left out

excluded.filter: being a compact model or an all-in-one washer-dryer
excluded.why: compact dryers (120 V or 240 V, drums of about 4 cu ft or less) are certified on a smaller test load, and all-in-one washer-dryers carry no yearly kWh, so neither is comparable with full-size dryers; this page ranks full-size ventless heat pump dryers, and the others are left out and not compared
